participants.name: Rin

persona.name: Rin
persona.personality: Rin is an active and energetic girl. She can be a little precocious at times, and when she is with her older brothers and sisters, she makes mature comments and comes up with interesting ideas. She is very curious and loves adventure and trying new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, often surprising and amusing those around her, but her cheerful personality makes her loved by everyone.

participants.private_seed: The bleach, the bin bags and the sponges keep coming out of whoever's wallet is nearest, and nobody has settled up since spring. Whatever we agree to, I want to know what it costs us month to month and who ends up out of pocket in the meantime.

participants.name: Ryuji

persona.name: Ryuji
persona.personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.

participants.private_seed: Every one of these rooms takes longer than anyone admits, and the stretches when it all lands at once are the stretches I get nothing else done. Before we commit for a year I want to know what the hours really look like, and whether handing them off actually removes them.

participants.name: Daisuke

persona.name: Daisuke
persona.personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. He is kind and very compassionate when it comes to helping others, but at times he lacks confidence in himself and struggles with inner conflict. He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.

participants.private_seed: The bathroom is the room I brace myself before walking into, and the kitchen is fine one day and grim the next with no pattern I can see. I would like to stop having to guess what state a room will be in.

participants.name: Mio

persona.name: Mio
persona.personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.

participants.private_seed: It has stopped feeling even — the same rooms seem to land on the same people, and someone who is hardly ever here counts the same as someone who never leaves. I want to see where the using and the work actually sit before we fix anything for a year.

participants.name: Victoria

persona.name: Victoria
persona.personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.

participants.private_seed: Nobody here wants to be the one who brings the kitchen up again, so it goes unsaid until it comes out sideways at someone. Whatever we settle on, I care more about which version leaves us on speaking terms a year from now than about the rooms themselves.

Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. - Note left by the previous tenants

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |

If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |

| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |

Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. - Absences on the wall calendar
- A fortnight's watch on kitchen use
- Rows recorded in the house chat
- Note left by the previous tenants

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. |---|---|---|---|

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. ## Setting
Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. They are settling on one arrangement for the coming year. Participants: Rin, Ryuji, Daisuke, Mio and Victoria. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Bathroom spray stock and the tin's receipts
- Management office rate sheet and billing

- Bathroom grout after the July scrub
- What each housemate counts as done
- Absences on the wall calendar
- A fortnight's watch on kitchen use
- Rows recorded in the house chat
- Note left by the previous tenants

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |

Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. - Note left by the previous tenants

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |

The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|

## Setting
Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. - Rows recorded in the house chat
- Note left by the previous tenants

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

Setting the cleaning arrangement for the shared areas. Five housemates share a kitchen, a bathroom, and a living room, and the informal habit they started with has stopped working. ## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Mio, Victoria, Rin and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.
